title: India-Japan Summit 2026: Both Nations Reaffirm Economic Security Partnership, Focus on Northeast India and AI
summary: India and Japan held a bilateral summit in 2026, with both sides reaffirming their shared commitment to economic security as a foundational pillar of the relationship. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal stated that Japan and India are working together to promote industry in India's Northeast. The two countries also deepened ties on AI and technology, with PM Modi and Japan's Takaichi engaging on digital cooperation. Energy ties were also highlighted as a key area of collaboration.
exam_angle: India-Japan bilateral relations are a recurring GS Paper 2 topic; key themes include the Special Strategic and Global Partnership, Act East Policy linkage, and economic security cooperation.
key_facts: India-Japan Summit held in 2026
Focus areas: economic security, Northeast India industrialisation, AI & technology, energy
Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal represented India on economic cooperation
India-Japan relation status: Special Strategic and Global Partnership

title: Defence Acquisition Council Approves Rs 52,000 Crore Military Procurement Including Anti-Drone Systems and Air Defence Missiles
summary: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by the Defence Minister, approved military procurement worth Rs 52,000 crore. The approved items include anti-drone systems, air defence missiles, and naval equipment. Additionally, 600 Hammer bombs and anti-tank missiles worth approximately Rs 5,000 crore are also in the pipeline for approval. This is part of India's continued push to modernise its armed forces and strengthen indigenous defence manufacturing.
exam_angle: DAC approvals are central to India's defence procurement policy and the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative in defence; relevant to GS Paper 3 (Defence/Security) and GS Paper 2 (Government policies).
key_facts: DAC approved Rs 52,000 crore worth of military procurement
Includes: anti-drone systems, air defence missiles, naval equipment
600 Hammer bombs and anti-tank missiles (Rs ~5,000 crore) also in pipeline
DAC is chaired by the Defence Minister of India

title: Monsoon Session of Parliament Scheduled to Begin July 20, 2026
summary: The Monsoon Session of the Indian Parliament has been set to commence on July 20, 2026. The session is expected to have a high-stakes legislative agenda. Parliamentary sessions are a key constitutional mechanism for legislative business, Question Hour, and government accountability. The timing aligns with the traditional monsoon session schedule.
exam_angle: Parliamentary sessions — Budget, Monsoon, and Winter — are important for Polity; the question of summoning Parliament (Article 85) and the role of sessions in law-making is frequently tested.
key_facts: Monsoon Session 2026 to begin: July 20
Parliament is summoned by the President under Article 85 of the Constitution
Three sessions annually: Budget (Feb), Monsoon (July), Winter (Nov-Dec)

title: Government Orders Removal of Three Chinese Battery Management Apps Used to Remotely Disable E-Rickshaws
summary: The Indian government ordered the removal of three Chinese battery management applications that were being used to remotely disable e-rickshaws — effectively acting as a 'kill switch.' The apps could lock the vehicles' batteries via a smartphone interface, creating disruption for drivers. The move is part of broader concerns about Chinese apps with potential security and economic vulnerabilities. The Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY) was involved in the action.
exam_angle: Connects to cybersecurity, data sovereignty, and regulation of Chinese apps in India (post-2020 ban context); relevant to GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech/Internal Security) and GS Paper 2 (Government policies).
key_facts: 3 Chinese battery management apps ordered to be removed
Apps used as remote 'kill switch' for e-rickshaw batteries
MeitY (Ministry of Electronics and IT) involved in action
Relates to India's ongoing scrutiny of Chinese digital applications

title: India Firms Up Position on Indus Waters Treaty Amid Pakistan Threats
summary: India has stated that its position on the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) remains 'unchanged' despite threats from Pakistan. This follows India's suspension/modification of its approach to the treaty after the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025. India has been asserting its rights over western rivers as well as pushing for treaty renegotiation. Pakistan has raised objections at global forums, with India preparing a strong rebuttal.
exam_angle: Indus Waters Treaty (1960, World Bank-mediated) is a perennial IR and environment topic; India-Pakistan water disputes are tested in GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Environment).
key_facts: Indus Waters Treaty signed in 1960, mediated by the World Bank
India declared treaty 'in abeyance' following Pahalgam attack (April 2025)
India reaffirms its stand remains 'unchanged' despite Pakistani pressure
Treaty allocates eastern rivers to India, western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan

title: India's Services PMI Falls to 17-Month Low of 57.4 in June 2026 as Demand Softens
summary: India's Services Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) dropped to 57.4 in June 2026, a 17-month low, as demand conditions softened. Despite the decline, any reading above 50 indicates expansion, so the services sector remains in growth territory. The slowdown is attributed to moderation in new business inflows. The Services PMI is compiled by S&P Global and tracks activity in the services sector.
exam_angle: PMI is a key economic indicator frequently referenced in GS Paper 3 (Economy); understanding the PMI threshold (50) and its sectoral significance is important for prelims and mains.
key_facts: India Services PMI: 57.4 in June 2026 (17-month low)
Any PMI above 50 signals expansion; below 50 signals contraction
PMI compiled by S&P Global (formerly IHS Markit)
Decline driven by softening of new business demand

title: New Gold Monetisation Scheme in the Works to Reduce Dependence on Imported Gold
summary: The Indian government is working on a revamped Gold Monetisation Scheme aimed at reducing India's heavy dependence on imported gold. The scheme will seek to mobilise idle domestic gold held by households and institutions. India is one of the world's largest gold importers, and the scheme is intended to channel domestic gold into the financial system. Details of the new scheme design are still being finalised.
exam_angle: Gold Monetisation Scheme (GMS) was originally launched in 2015; its revision connects to GS Paper 3 (Economy) themes of current account deficit, gold imports, and government schemes.
key_facts: Original Gold Monetisation Scheme launched in 2015
New scheme aims to reduce gold import dependence
India is among the world's top gold importers (approx. 700-800 tonnes/year)
Scheme mobilises idle household/institutional gold into banking system

title: MeitY Summons Meta Over Instagram Ads Promoting Child Sexual Abuse Material in India
summary: A BBC investigation found that Instagram was running advertisements in India that promoted child sexual abuse material (CSAM). IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw ordered MeitY to summon Meta to explain the lapse. The incident raises serious concerns about platform accountability under India's IT Rules 2021 and the Information Technology Act. Meta is required to ensure due diligence and content moderation under its obligations as a significant social media intermediary.
exam_angle: Relates to IT Act 2000, IT (Intermediary Guidelines) Rules 2021, digital governance and platform accountability — core GS Paper 2 (Polity/Governance) and GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech) topics.
key_facts: BBC investigation revealed Instagram ads promoting CSAM in India
IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw ordered MeitY to summon Meta
Governed by IT Act 2000 and IT (Intermediary Guidelines) Rules 2021
Meta (parent of Instagram) is classified as a Significant Social Media Intermediary (SSMI)

title: India Issues Notices to WhatsApp, Telegram, and Signal Over Anonymity and Username Features
summary: After sending a notice to Meta over WhatsApp's new username feature, the Indian government has now issued notices to Telegram and Signal over their anonymity features. The Centre is examining whether these features comply with India's IT Rules 2021, which require significant social media intermediaries to enable traceability of message originators. The move is part of broader concerns about encryption and anonymity enabling illegal activities.
exam_angle: Traceability requirements under IT Rules 2021, encryption debate, and intermediary liability are critical GS Paper 2 and GS Paper 3 topics; also connects to Supreme Court's privacy jurisprudence.
key_facts: Notices issued to WhatsApp, Telegram, and Signal
Issue: username/anonymity features potentially enabling untraceable communication
IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules 2021 require traceability
Significant Social Media Intermediaries (SSMIs) must identify first originator of messages

title: Ethanol-Blended Fuel Row: Government Moves to Quell Public Backlash After 'Experiment' Remark
summary: The Indian government moved to manage public backlash over ethanol-blended petrol after a remark describing the blending programme as an 'experiment' sparked controversy. India has a national target of 20% ethanol blending in petrol by 2025-26 under the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) programme. The government reiterated its commitment to the programme, which aims to reduce oil imports, cut emissions, and boost farmer incomes. The blending programme is also aligned with India's energy security and climate goals.
exam_angle: Ethanol blending programme is a key GS Paper 3 topic (Economy + Environment); connects to energy security, farm income support, and India's NDC commitments under Paris Agreement.
key_facts: India's target: 20% ethanol blending in petrol by 2025-26 under EBP Programme
Ethanol sourced primarily from sugarcane, maize, and damaged food grains
Programme reduces crude oil imports and lowers vehicular emissions
Nodal ministry: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

title: Ayatollah Khamenei Dies: India Pays Tribute as Iran Holds State Funeral in Tehran
summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei passed away and was laid in state in Tehran ahead of a weeklong mass funeral. Indian dignitaries paid tribute to the late Iranian Supreme Leader. Khamenei had held the position of Supreme Leader since 1989 following Ayatollah Khomeini. His son Mojtaba Khamenei's absence from the funeral drew attention amid speculation about succession. The development has significant geopolitical implications for West Asia and India-Iran relations.
exam_angle: Iran's political structure (Supreme Leader, President, Guardian Council) and India-Iran bilateral relations (Chabahar Port, energy ties) are important GS Paper 2 (IR) topics.
key_facts: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei: Iran's Supreme Leader since 1989
Supreme Leader is the highest authority in Iran's theocratic system
India-Iran ties: Chabahar Port, energy imports, connectivity to Central Asia
Succession question: Iran's Assembly of Experts appoints the next Supreme Leader

title: France Records 30% Rise in Deaths During June 2026 Heatwave: Report
summary: France reported a 30% rise in deaths during the June 2026 heatwave, according to official data. The heatwave is part of a broader pattern of extreme heat events intensifying across Europe due to climate change. European countries have been witnessing record-breaking temperatures with increasing frequency. The report underscores the public health and mortality dimensions of climate-induced extreme weather events.
exam_angle: Heatwaves as a climate change impact, urban heat island effect, and extreme weather mortality are important for GS Paper 3 (Environment) and GS Paper 1 (Geography).
key_facts: France: 30% rise in deaths during June 2026 heatwave
Heatwaves are classified as extreme weather events linked to climate change
IPCC reports indicate frequency and intensity of heatwaves increasing globally
Heat mortality is a key public health concern in the context of climate adaptation

title: Russia Purchased Gasoline Produced by India's Nayara Energy via Third-Party Traders: Report
summary: Fuel-hit Russia reportedly purchased gasoline produced by India's Nayara Energy through third-party traders, according to media reports. Nayara Energy is a Rosneft-backed refinery based in Vadinar, Gujarat. This development is significant as it reveals the indirect channels through which sanctioned Russia continues to access petroleum products. India has maintained that its energy trade with Russia does not violate any applicable sanctions.
exam_angle: India-Russia energy trade, Western sanctions on Russia, and India's strategic autonomy in foreign policy are key GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Economy/Energy) topics.
key_facts: Nayara Energy: major Indian refinery, backed by Russia's Rosneft
Located in Vadinar, Gujarat; one of India's largest private refineries
Russia under Western sanctions since 2022 Ukraine invasion
India maintains energy trade does not violate applicable international sanctions

title: India Investigates Tata Electronics Data Leak That Exposed Apple iPhone Manufacturing Secrets
summary: Indian authorities are investigating a data leak from Tata Electronics that reportedly exposed sensitive Apple iPhone manufacturing data and trade secrets. Tata Electronics, a subsidiary of the Tata Group, manufactures iPhones in India as part of Apple's efforts to diversify its supply chain away from China. The breach raises concerns about data security in critical manufacturing supply chains. Apple and Tata Electronics are key players in India's electronics manufacturing ecosystem under the PLI scheme.
exam_angle: Connects to India's PLI scheme for electronics manufacturing, data security, cybersecurity law, and supply chain diversification — relevant to GS Paper 3 (Economy/Sci-Tech).
key_facts: Tata Electronics manufactures iPhones in India (PLI scheme beneficiary)
Data leak allegedly exposed Apple iPhone manufacturing secrets
Investigation underway by Indian authorities
Apple's India manufacturing: part of China+1 supply chain diversification strategy

title: Supreme Court Refuses to Cancel Bail of Sonam Raghuvanshi in Meghalaya Honeymoon Murder Case
summary: The Supreme Court of India declined to cancel the bail granted to Sonam Raghuvanshi, the accused in the Meghalaya honeymoon murder case. The court maintained that the bail order would continue. The case involves allegations of murder of a husband during a honeymoon trip in Meghalaya. The Supreme Court's decision reflects the high threshold required to cancel bail once granted by a lower court.
exam_angle: Bail jurisprudence under CrPC (now BNSS), Supreme Court's appellate powers, and personal liberty under Article 21 are important GS Paper 2 (Polity) and judicial process topics.
key_facts: Supreme Court refused to stay/cancel bail of Sonam Raghuvanshi
Case: Meghalaya honeymoon murder — alleged murder of husband
Bail cancellation requires higher threshold than bail grant (settled SC jurisprudence)
Relates to Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty) and bail under BNSS 2023

title: 8th Pay Commission: Projections Show Basic Pay Could Rise from Rs 18,000 to Rs 69,000
summary: Speculative projections on the 8th Pay Commission suggest that the minimum basic pay for central government employees could rise from Rs 18,000 to approximately Rs 69,000, implying a fitment factor of around 2.86. The 8th Pay Commission was constituted in January 2025 and is expected to submit its recommendations, which would be implemented from January 2026. The commission reviews pay, allowances, and service conditions of central government employees.
exam_angle: Pay Commissions are significant for GS Paper 3 (Economy) — they impact government expenditure, fiscal deficit, and consumption demand; also relevant to governance (GS Paper 2).
key_facts: 8th Pay Commission constituted: January 2025
Implementation expected from: January 2026
Current minimum basic pay (7th CPC): Rs 18,000
Projected fitment factor speculation: ~2.86x (implying ~Rs 69,000 minimum basic pay)

title: NIFT Mumbai Participates in HGH India 2026 to Showcase Academic and Industry Connect
summary: The National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT) Mumbai participated in HGH India 2026, a leading home, housewares, and gift trade fair, to showcase its academic excellence and industry linkages. NIFT is a statutory body established under the NIFT Act 2006 under the Ministry of Textiles. The participation underscores the role of design education institutions in connecting with India's textile and handicraft industries. HGH India is one of Asia's largest trade fairs for home and lifestyle products.
exam_angle: NIFT as a statutory institution under the Ministry of Textiles, and government initiatives linking design education to industry, are relevant for GS Paper 2 (Governance) and GS Paper 1 (Culture/Art).
key_facts: NIFT: established under NIFT Act 2006, under Ministry of Textiles
NIFT Mumbai participated in HGH India 2026 trade fair
HGH India: major trade fair for home, housewares, and gift sector
NIFT has 19 campuses across India
